title: The Software Crisis Behind America's Infrastructure

reader_summary.headline: If you don't have the sense of urgency, we're not going to help you what we need to do.
reader_summary.overview: If you don't have the sense of urgency, we're not going to help you what we need to do. You can build the most advanced equipment. You can produce it at the largest scale possible. But if you can't get it, where it's needed, when it's needed, it doesn't exist.

key_points.text: There's always been collective defense, but not necessary collective logistics.
key_points.evidence_quote: There's always been collective defense, but not necessary collective logistics.

key_points.text: Whatever we're modernizing now, this is not going to be the last update.

thesis: The podcast argues that a software crisis exists because critical infrastructure in both public and private sectors relies on legacy technology that is becoming increasingly brittle as the world moves at the speed of software. This brittleness causes inconveniences at best and tragedies at worst, necessitating a modernization effort where the public and private sectors join forces via dual-use software to harden America's logistical network.
